text:
I live so free of love, and have lived so,
that willingly I taste its pain,
giving exercise to all the resistance
that rests within my hardened breast.

I gaze upon the flame from a safe distance,
by freedom's habit, not by prudence;
for beauty, whose appearance is its soul,
needs only the risk to one sense.

Let him flee the sea who, safe on shore,
saw the clear dangers of the drowned;
let him not trust the sea for a divine light.

For heaven reserves its mercy
for one who groans, bound to his ruin,
not for him who builds his own.

translation.title: I Live So Free of Love
